architecture.mechanism: Robotics-assisted inspection combined with AI-supported predictive operation and maintenance for corrosion and fatigue degradation in offshore wind support structures.
architecture.intervention: Deploy remotely operated vehicle (ROV)-based cathodic-protection potential mapping and wall-thickness ultrasonic scanning on the monopile splash and submerged zones, with AI-driven corrosion-rate prediction models fed into a digital twin, eliminating sacrificial anodes and diver inspections.
architecture.expected_effect: Early detection of coating breakdown and wall-thickness loss enables just-in-life targeted coating repair and ICCP current adjustment, avoiding full cathodic anode replacement; keeps lifecycle inspection and mitigation cost below the $50,000/foundation/decade North Sea budget.
architecture.falsification_test: Instrument a North Sea monopile with ROV-mounted CP and ultrasonic sensors for 5 years, run the AI predictive model against actual measured wall loss, and compare accumulated inspection-plus-mitigation costs to a sacrificial-anode baseline; fail criterion is actual cost exceeding $50,000/decade or undetected corrosion loss exceeding 0.3 mm/yr.
